title: Our game flopped in play testing, so we extracted our map editor for free general use
author: loves_typescript
selftext:
When my studio set out to make a game, we really picked a large one to chew on; a game we had to teach people computer science to play. Long story short, we didn't make our release date - but what we did make was a pretty good in-house level editor based on the Tiled file format.

Our free map editor, **Tauric Studio**, is that work extracted into a standalone tool. Here are the features we built that you might find useful in your own studio's pipeline:

\- Full Tiled map compatibility for finite and infinite tile maps.

\- Full drop-in Aseprite file compatibility; see your sprites in your level at scale.

\- Custom entity type library lives in project configuration so you can stamp your enemies down at a predictable size.

\- Pretty decent vector eding.

\- Wide import/export support across multiple vector/raster formats.

\- Real time multiplayer.

\- It's completely web-based.

Anyway, we're straight-up trying to productize this, but it's currently being provided as a free web service at [https://tauric.tools](https://tauric.tools). Posting here because I want feedback about the tool.

replies.author: loves_typescript
replies.body: It is called "Open Sourcerer". It's not cancelled, but we're trying to find a way to put something else forward in the short term.
